newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia signs deal to supply LNG to Japex.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia signs deal to supply LNG to Japex.

text.p: A joint venture company of Malaysian national oil firm Petronas has signed a letter of intent with Japan Petroleum Exploration Co Ltd (Japex) to supply liquefied natural gas, Petronas said on Tuesday.

The joint venture firm, Malaysia LNG Tiga Sdn Bhd, would supply up to 1.5 million tonnes of liquefied natural gas a year for 20 years, beginning in 2001 using tankers owned by Petronas Tankers Sdn Bhd, Petronas said in a statement.
The LNG project is located in Bintulu in eastern Sarawak state and is designed to produce 6.8 million tonnes a year.
Malaysia LNG Tiga is a joint venture between Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), the Sarawak state government, Nippon Oil Co Ltd, Occidental LNG (Malaysia) Ltd and Shell Gas B.V..
Japex is 65.74 percent owned by Japan National Oil Corp and currently markets crude oil to refineries and natural gas to power plants, chemical plants and city gas distributors, Petronas said.
Japex has built a total of 250 km of gas trunklines across the island of Honshu from Niigata to Sendai, which started operations in 1996.
